Chapter 10: Legacy, Impact, and the Meaning of Creative Work.
As the years roll by and the dust finally settles, we start to wonder—what does it really mean to leave a mark? Is it about the number of users you’ve reached, the size of your company, or those shiny awards on a shelf? Or is it actually something softer, quieter... maybe a ripple of influence that spreads out in ways you never even see?
Think about this: there’s a moment you might remember, meeting someone whose life was changed by something simple—a tool you built, a piece of advice you gave, or just a bit of encouragement. You don’t always see the impact, but that doesn’t make it any less real. Most of us have no clue how far the effects of our work might travel, or just how many people we touch without ever realizing it.
I want to share a story with you. There’s this mentor—late in his career—who gets a message out of the blue from an old colleague. Turns out, a few kind words he shared years ago gave that colleague the courage to follow his own dreams. The mentor? He’s genuinely humbled. And he’s reminded that the true value of creative work isn’t about being famous or stacking up money—it’s about the lives you help change along the way.
So what is legacy, really? It’s not about being remembered for the sake of it. It’s about making a difference, even if it’s in small, everyday ways—helping out, sharing what you know, or just creating with honesty and heart. A lot of people miss how much power they’ve got to shape the world, one small act at a time.
When you look back, you start to realize—the journey isn’t just about the big wins or the tough setbacks. It’s about the relationships you’ve built, the risks you were willing to take, and that inner drive to keep moving forward. If you ever wonder what your work is really worth, here’s something to hold onto: focus on the impact you make, not just the recognition you get.
Because, in the end, your real legacy? It’s the difference you make in the lives of others.
